subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 42-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus (body mass index 33) takes metformin and basal insulin. During 40 minutes of moderate cycling, his continuous glucose monitor falls from 198 mg/dL to 128 mg/dL although he ate no food and took no prandial insulin for 5 hours; plasma insulin is 18 mIU/L before exercise and 17 mIU/L afterward.
question: The exercise-induced fall in his glucose is best explained by translocation of which of the following transporters to the skeletal muscle plasma membrane?

options.text: GLUT4, through AMP-activated protein kinase signaling

explanation_correct: Skeletal muscle and adipose tissue express GLUT4, which is stored in intracellular vesicles and translocates to the plasma membrane in response to insulin. Contracting muscle also translocates GLUT4 through AMPK-dependent signaling, so glucose uptake rises during exercise even when insulin concentrations do not change, which explains the fall in glucose in this insulin-resistant patient.

explanation_incorrect.B: GLUT1 is constitutively present on most cell membranes and responds to neither insulin nor exercise, so it cannot account for contraction-stimulated glucose uptake.
explanation_incorrect.C: GLUT2 is a high-Km, bidirectional transporter of liver and pancreatic beta cells and does not mediate contraction-stimulated glucose uptake in muscle.
explanation_incorrect.D: SGLT2 is confined to the proximal renal tubule and does not transport glucose into skeletal muscle.
explanation_incorrect.E: GLUT3 is a high-affinity, insulin-independent transporter of neurons and placenta and is not responsible for exercise-induced muscle uptake.

educationalObjective: Exercise and insulin both increase skeletal muscle glucose uptake by translocating GLUT4, but exercise acts through AMPK and does not require insulin.
